points.description: Role of the learning rate: it controls the step size/speed of convergence (small rate gives slow convergence; larger rate gives faster convergence, possibly oscillating/zigzagging).
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says it affects learning/convergence without mentioning speed or step size.

points.description: Danger: if the learning rate is too high (exceeds a critical value), learning becomes unstable/diverges (oscillation or zigzagging may be mentioned).
points.partial_credit: Half if only mentions zigzagging/oscillation or overshooting without instability or divergence, or only says too-small rate is slow.

rubric.notes: Full marks: says the learning rate sets the step size/speed of convergence, and that too large a rate causes instability/divergence (or overshooting). Part marks: vague answers, e.g. only slow vs fast, or only zigzagging without instability. No marks for unrelated or wrong claims. Technical terms like overdamped/underdamped are not required.
